title: Market prices key is "optional" on first run and a required step afterwards
body:
## Summary
The approval window's first-run view calls the market-prices key optional, then its everyday view counts it as a thing left to set up, in gold.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/OwnerConfig.tsx:273 labels the channel3 credential "optional" and never gold while first run shows; lib/firstRun.ts START_ORDER has no market step. After first run, OwnerConfig.tsx:215-218 counts it among four required steps ("1 thing left to set up · Still to do: Market prices") and gold={!first} marks it needed. One key, two claims. Which is true is a product decision: if comparing prices is optional, drop it from `steps`/`left`; if it is needed, first run should say so.

## Flow
- New owner completes the four first-run steps without a market key (told optional)
- first-run view gives way to the everyday view
- the answer bar now reads "1 thing left to set up · Still to do: Market prices" with a gold Needed chip

## Expected impact
One consistent answer about whether the price key is needed. Could break: nothing either way.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one claim about one key
Before: 2 contradictory claims (OwnerConfig.tsx:273 vs :215-218)
After: 1
Method: probe - read both branches and lib/firstRun START_ORDER
Result: better
Gate: direction

title: check_lever, RescueContext and discounted have no caller: delete or wire R1
body:
## Summary
The R1 retry rule (check_lever, RescueContext, discounted and three RescueError variants) is tested but called by nothing; the levers it guards cannot be signed.

## Description
crates/table-core/src/rescue.rs:13-65 holds check_lever (retry refused on REPLAY or within 24 h, capture <= outstanding), RescueContext and discounted. A grep over crates, services and the client finds no caller outside rescue.rs tests; validate refuses every lever but DISCOUNT_THIS_CYCLE (mandate.rs "only the discount this cycle is available"), and the discount path uses propose_discount/check_offer. The code encodes acceptance R1 (docs/design/the-table.extract.txt:938) for levers that are not built. Deleting it is verified dead code (~55 lines + a test) but drops the only executable statement of R1; keeping it leaves a policy that reads as enforced and is not. That is a product call.

## Flow
- grep check_lever|RescueContext|discounted( across crates, services, client -> rescue.rs only
- option A: delete, keep R1 in the design doc
- option B: keep, mark staged-for-the-lever in STATUS.md

## Expected impact
Either the dead surface goes, or it is labelled as staged. Removal breaks no consumer (0 found).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no policy code that looks enforced and is not
Before: 3 pub items + 3 error variants, 0 callers
After: A: 0 / B: same code, documented as staged
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep run this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
grep -rn "check_lever|RescueContext|discounted(" crates services apps --include=*.rs --include=*.ts -> crates/table-core/src/rescue.rs only
crates/table-core/src/mandate.rs only the discount this cycle is available
impact: Either the dead surface goes, or it is labelled as staged. Removal breaks no consumer (0 found).
instrument: none needed for A beyond cargo check --workspace --all-targets; the decision is which option

title: The type-the-name step before unpausing a scam-check hold is enforced only in the window
body:
## Summary
Releasing a shield HOLD asks the owner to type the payee's name exactly; Rust's shield_release takes DecisionArgs with no name, so the friction is a client-only narrowing any other caller of the command skips.

## Description
gating.ts:187-192 enables releaseHold only when namesMatch(typed, expectedName); DealReview.tsx:480-501 renders the typer. crates/table-runtime/src/service.rs decide(ReleaseHold) checks token, label, unlock, selection, terms, attempt and the checklist (shield line exempt) but receives no typed name (bindings/DecisionArgs.ts has deal_id, attempt, terms_hash, checks_hash, counter_hash). The approval window is the only UI that holds the capability, so the gap is defence in depth, not an open door. Enforcing it in Rust means a new DecisionArgs field and an authority/binding change (AGENTS.md IPC procedure), and deciding whether the name check is a security control or a UX speed bump is the owner's call.

## Flow
- owner opens a HOLD deal; window requires the typed name
- a privileged shield_release call with valid DecisionArgs and no name is accepted by Rust
- option: add typed_name to the release args and compare it in decide(ReleaseHold) against the counterparty display

## Expected impact
Makes the confirmation a property of the wallet, not of one page. Could break: every caller and the mock must send the name; PINNED_MANIFEST unchanged (args, not authority).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the release confirmation is enforced where the decision is made
Before: typed-name check on 1 of 2 layers (client only)
After: predicted 2 of 2
Method: simulation - read gating.ts, DealReview.tsx and service.rs decide(); a contract change was out of this round's scope
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/gating.ts:191 `(namesMatch(ctx.typedName, ctx.expectedName) ? null : ...)`
crates/table-runtime/src/service.rs:653-657 Decision::ReleaseHold => record + owner_release_hold(deal.id, args.attempt, ticket, now) (no name)

title: Make the window's and the wallet's "by day" lines use one calendar
body:
> Lane B unmeasurable: escalate contract - BookQuery day offset vs owner local-day semantics (37/500 deals differ)

## Summary
Ask's two tables group "by day" differently: the window by the owner's local day, the wallet by the UTC day, so 37 of 500 large-world deals sit on different days in the two tables (UTC+2).

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/book/model.ts:111-115 dayKey uses local getDate(); crates/table-ledger/src/book.rs:56 groups by date(created_at,'unixepoch') (UTC). Ask.tsx shows both tables for one question (Pivot and WalletAnswer), and the CSV day column uses the local key. Typed ranges are already worked out in the owner's calendar (understand.ts whenSpan), so the wallet's grouping is the odd one out. Fixed: the BookQuery carries the owner's UTC offset (or the client groups by the wallet's UTC day and says so); either is an in-tree contract change (table-core BookQuery, bindings, mock backend) with a verifier to write.

## Flow
- owner at UTC+2 asks "What happened each day?"
- a deal created at 01:00 local on day D+1 (23:00 UTC on day D) is on D+1 in the window table and on D in the wallet table
- window table and wallet table give different counts per day for the same question

## Expected impact
The two tables under one answer agree line for line. Could break: every BookQuery consumer if a field is added (contract).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - deals grouped on the same day by both tables
Before: probe (large world, TZ offset -120): 37 of 500 deals have dayKey != UTC date
After: predicted 0 of 500; not built: crates/table-ledger is outside this round and BookQuery is a contract
Method: probe - vitest over the large mock world comparing dayKey with toISOString().slice(0,10)
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: direction.test.ts-style test: a deal at 00:30 local in a UTC+2 calendar; window day line and mock book_query day line must name the same day (mock mirrors book.rs)

title: A less-cautious shield raise turns a terms-bound HOLD into a permanent one
body:
## Summary
raise_shield_for, given a verdict below a computed (terms-bound) HOLD, rewrites the row with shield_terms NULL, so the price HOLD becomes a 'raised' one that no reprice and no later CLEAR can clear.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/src/shield.rs:174-192: for a stored computed HOLD (terms set, not raised) and a raised ASK, the match falls to `Some(old) => (old, s.rule)` but write() is called with terms None. The deal now reads as a raised HOLD (Stored::raised, shield.rs:36), so the projection keeps it across a terms change and record_shield's raised branch (shield.rs:119-123) refuses every lower computed verdict. The second opinion only wanted 'at least ASK'; the owner instead gets a price_over_market HOLD on a price that is no longer the deal's. A correct fix needs the raised floor and the computed verdict stored apart (one verdict column today), i.e. a schema change, or a policy choice to drop one of them.

## Flow
- record_shield(HOLD, price_over_market, terms T) -> computed hold
- raise_shield(ASK) (second opinion) -> row rewritten HOLD/price_over_market, terms NULL
- reprice -> deal still held; record_shield(CLEAR, new terms) returns false
- control without the ASK raise: reprice drops the hold (shield None, not held)

## Expected impact
Owners whose second opinion returns ASK on a deal the price rule already held see a hold naming a price rule after the price changed and must release it by hand. A fix that keeps terms instead would lose the model's ASK floor on a terms change (policy-loosen).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a computed HOLD stays tied to its terms after a lower raise
Before: probe (temporary test, removed): after HOLD(T) + raise ASK + reprice: held=true, shield=HOLD, rule=price_over_market; CLEAR on new terms wrote=false, still held. Control (no raise): held=false, shield=None.
After: not built: either a second column for the raised floor (migration) or a policy choice which caution survives
Method: probe - temporary test in shield_tests.rs run and reverted; the gate rung needs the design choice first
Result: better
Gate: irreversible
evidence:
crates/table-ledger/src/shield.rs:174
crates/table-ledger/src/shield.rs:184-192 (write(.., None, ..))
crates/table-ledger/src/shield.rs:119-123
PROBE held=true shield=Some(Hold) rule=Some(PriceOverMarket)
PROBE after CLEAR wrote=false held=true
CONTROL held=false shield=None
instrument: shield_tests: record_shield HOLD(T) -> raise_shield ASK -> reprice -> assert the price hold no longer holds (only the raise's ASK floor) and record_shield CLEAR(T') writes

title: Release builds discard every runtime diagnostic
body:
## Summary
The runtime writes its diagnostics with eprintln!, but the release desktop app runs under windows_subsystem="windows", where stderr goes nowhere. ladder.rs's doc comment says a failed rung is 'logged'.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/configuration.rs:519 and crates/table-runtime/src/ladder.rs:43 use eprintln!; apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:1 sets windows_subsystem="windows" for release; crates/table-runtime/src/ladder.rs:5 claims 'logged and dropped'. The product has no log crate or sink, so choosing one (rolling file, audit row, event) is a product decision.

## Flow
- release build, a rung write fails
- eprintln! goes to a detached stderr
- no trace anywhere

## Expected impact
Support can see why a rung or a credential date was not recorded. Possible breakage: the sink must never carry secrets or counterparty text.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - a diagnostic sink exists
Before: 2 production eprintln! sites with no sink in release
After: a chosen sink
Method: simulation - a decision, not a measurement
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:1 #![cfg_attr(all(windows, not(debug_assertions)), windows_subsystem = "windows")]; crates/table-runtime/src/ladder.rs:43 eprintln!("The Table: an attention rung could not be recorded");

title: Project Rust’s per-clause gate verdicts to the Main window
body:
## Summary
The "Rules that applied" view reconstructs each clause verdict by client arithmetic (or "unknown") because Rust does not project its per-clause gate results to Main; each reading is a second implementation of the gate that can disagree with it.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/deal/model.ts:5-8 records the decision; model.ts:174-224 re-derives roles, pinned/house counterparties, per-deal limit, band and threshold, and marks velocity, payees and lever unknown. The clause-6 card in this file is one measured disagreement. Fixed: a read-tier IPC field carrying Rust’s verdict per clause for a deal, which readClauses displays instead of computing.

## Flow
- add a per-clause verdict projection (deal_display or a new read command: authority table row, bindings, PINNED_MANIFEST)
- readClauses shows it; arithmetic stays only as a labelled fallback

## Expected impact
The owner sees the gate’s own verdicts. Could break: the IPC contract and its pinned manifest.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for clause verdicts
Before: 9 clause kinds, 5 computed client-side, 4 unknown or not-applicable
After: 9 from Rust (predicted)
Method: simulation - a contract change, not buildable in a client round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract

title: The engine's Job Object sets no process-count or memory budget
body:
> Lane B unmeasurable: Job Object caps must come from the live engine spike (operator-only)

## Summary
The kill-on-close Job Object holding every native child sets only JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so a child tree can spawn and allocate without bound until the 120 s ceiling.

## Description
crates/table-engine/src/windows_job.rs:51 sets LimitFlags = JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE only: no ActiveProcessLimit, JobMemoryLimit or ProcessMemoryLimit. The CLIs are third-party binaries that may load user mods (.research/landscape-and-stack.md 2.1: the CLI permission layer is advisory), on a desktop the wallet shares. Registry subprocess-lifecycle host-resource-protection: 'budgets are per-child ... terminated by policy, not discovered by the host's own death'. Stdout volume is already capped (read_lines, 4 MiB); process count and memory are not.

## Flow
- a child (or a mod it loads) forks repeatedly or allocates several GB
- the job holds them all until the 120 s ceiling, or the machine starves first
- fix: JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_ACTIVE_PROCESS and JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_JOB_MEMORY in the same SetInformationJobObject call
- instrument: engine-fixture modes 'fanout' and 'alloc' the job must stop

## Expected impact
A runaway agent app cannot take the wallet's machine down with it. Could break: a real CLI that legitimately needs more processes - the live spike must confirm the numbers.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - per-child resource budget
Before: job limits: 1 flag (kill-on-close); a fixture spawning 64 descendants keeps all of them alive (walked)
After: fanout past the cap fails to spawn, alloc past the cap is killed; cleanup tests still green
Method: simulation - needs two fixture modes and Win32 limit fields; the numbers need the live spike
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: crates/table-engine/src/bin/engine-fixture.rs modes fanout/alloc + crates/table-engine/tests/native.rs asserting the run ends with the tree dead and memory bounded

title: A codex tool call without arguments passes the parser; a claude one fails
body:
> Lane B unmeasurable: no recorded real codex stream in the repo (operator-only, spike 1)

## Summary
The stream parser rejects a claude tool_use with no input as Invalid but turns a codex mcp_tool_call with no arguments into a ToolCall with null arguments.

## Description
crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:135 `c.get("input").cloned().ok_or(Error::Invalid)?` vs crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:188 `v.pointer("/item/arguments").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)`. One rule (a tool call names its arguments), two implementations, under a crate doc that promises strict stream validation. Whether real codex item.started events always carry `arguments` is not in .research (only the synthetic fixture), so tightening could break a real stream: decide it from a recorded codex stream.

## Flow
- codex emits item.started mcp_tool_call without arguments
- crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:188 yields ToolCall { arguments: null }
- claude's equivalent yields Err(Invalid) and poisons the run
- fix: ok_or(Error::Invalid) on the codex side once a recorded stream shows arguments is always present

## Expected impact
Both adapters judge the same malformed call the same way. Could break: a real codex stream that omits arguments on item.started.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule, one behaviour
Before: claude missing input -> Err; codex missing arguments -> Ok(null) (walked)
After: both -> Err(Invalid); the e1 conformance suite covers the case for both engines
Method: simulation - the premise about codex's real shape needs a recorded stream (spike 1)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: crates/table-engine/tests/engine.rs: e1 suite case 'tool call without arguments' for both engines expecting Err (codex passes today), checked against a recorded codex stream

title: Codex's documented item.failed and error events poison a run
body:
## Summary
The codex branch of the stream parser rejects `item.failed` and `item.updated` and treats a non-terminal `error` as the run's end.

## Description
crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:201-212 makes `error` terminal and crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:214 `_ => Err(Error::Invalid)` rejects every other type. .research/landscape-and-stack.md:203 lists item.started|item.completed|item.failed as sourced [S] codex events and turn.failed, item.updated, error as recalled [R]. A failed MCP item or a retried-then-recovered stream ends the run as isolation_or_stream_failure. Codex cannot start at all today (no system/init; the probe reports unavailable), so the fix belongs with the attestation redesign and must be decided from a recorded codex stream.

## Flow
- codex reports a failed wallet call as item.failed
- crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:214 -> Err(Invalid); the run is poisoned
- after a recorded stream: item.failed for a wallet tool -> no event; error terminal only when it really ends the turn

## Expected impact
A codex run survives its own documented events once it can run at all. Could break: the fence, if item.failed can name a non-wallet tool - keep the check.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - documented events do not poison runs
Before: item.failed -> Err(Invalid) (walked)
After: item.failed for a wallet tool -> no event, the run continues
Method: simulation - needs a live codex stream; the operator-only spike 1 is the rung above
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:201-212 "turn.failed" | "error" => terminal
crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:214 _ => Err(Error::Invalid)
.research/landscape-and-stack.md:203 item.failed [S]; error, item.updated [R]
instrument: operator-only: scripts/spike.ps1 -Spike 1 recording the codex stream, then a crates/table-engine/tests/fixtures replay

title: Drop the debug-only loopback navigation allowance that no config uses
body:
## Summary
Debug builds let every webview navigate to any port on localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1], but the app never loads from a dev server.

## Description
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native/navigation.rs:16 allows http(s) loopback on any port when cfg!(debug_assertions); navigation_tests.rs:79-85 pins it. tauri.conf.json has no build.devUrl and scripts/dev/tauri-dev-test.mjs runs cargo run with the embedded dist, so the allowance has 0 users while any local service is reachable from a debug webview. Removing it narrows debug builds, but it is the owner's deliberate dev affordance, so the call is theirs (direction).

## Flow
- debug build: a webview navigates to http://127.0.0.1:<any>/ -> allowed
- release build: refused (unchanged)
- fix: delete the loopback arm and flip loopback_dev_server_is_debug_only to refuse

## Expected impact
Debug builds stop reaching local services from the app windows; no release change. Breaks a future dev-server workflow until devUrl is added with its own rule.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - debug navigation matches what the app loads
Before: any loopback port navigable in debug, 0 configured users (grep devUrl: 0)
After: app origin only
Method: probe - grep for devUrl / dev server in config and scripts
Result: better
Gate: direction
instrument: navigation_tests: loopback refused with dev=true; grep devUrl in tauri.conf.json and scripts -> 0

title: Domain-tag the HOUSE table answer and release-pin signatures
body:
## Summary
Two signatures in the HOUSE trust path carry no domain tag: the agent's signature over a HouseResponse (crates/table-proto/src/house.rs:97-99, 130-136) and the owner's release-pin signature over the raw 32-byte mandate commitment (house.rs:38-41), which is the same message form as a HELLO's owner_sig_over_commitment (envelope.rs:233-235).

## Description
Every newer signature in this crate is domain-separated: heads and prefixes (house_ledger.rs:156-159, 217-225), owner accepts ('table.owner.accept.v1', envelope.rs:107-114), pairing JWS headers (pairing.rs:31). The agent key also signs JWS inputs, closed mandates, pairing identities and raw commitments; the owner key signs mandates, wallet envelopes and raw commitments. No live collision was found (a HouseResponse's canonical bytes are a 3-element array no other signed form produces, and pins are compiled in, never accepted off the wire), so this is defence in depth per signed-artifacts/canonical-hashing. Adding a tag changes bytes that shipped wallets and the hosted HOUSE verify: a versioned wire change with readers outside this tree.

## Flow
- agent key signs canonical (seller, mandate, table) with no tag
- owner key signs the raw commitment, identical to a HELLO commitment signature
- a future signed form that encodes to the same bytes would verify as the other

## Expected impact
Closes cross-protocol signature reuse by construction. Breaks every wallet build and HOUSE release that verifies the untagged form unless both forms are accepted for a transition window.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every signature in the HOUSE path is domain-separated
Before: 2 of 6 signature kinds in house.rs/house_ledger.rs/envelope.rs untagged
After: 0 of 6 (with a v2 form and a transition)
Method: simulation - enumerated the signed forms per key; a wire change cannot be verified against out-of-tree readers here
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
crates/table-proto/src/house.rs:97-99 canonical_bytes(&(&self.seller, &self.mandate, &self.table)) - no tag
crates/table-proto/src/house.rs:38-41 verify_strict(&self.mandate_commitment.0, owner_signature)
crates/table-proto/src/envelope.rs:233-235 owner.verify_strict(&mandate_commitment.0, &sig) (HELLO)
crates/table-proto/src/house_ledger.rs:156-159 HOUSE_HEAD_DOMAIN / HOUSE_PREFIX_DOMAIN (tagged)
instrument: n/a - external contract (the hosted HOUSE and shipped wallets verify these bytes); needs a decision on a v2 form and a transition window

title: CI installs and builds the client three times per push
body:
> Lane B demoted: needs a verified actions/download-artifact SHA pin and two real CI runs (operator-only)

## Summary
The client job and both legs of the rust matrix each run pnpm install and pnpm build for apps/desktop/client.

## Description
.github/workflows/ci.yml:21,24 (client job) and :51-52 in the rust job, whose matrix (:38) runs windows-latest and ubuntu-latest: 3 `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and 3 `pnpm build` (each a full tsc + vite build) per push. The rust legs need only dist/ to embed. Fixed: the client job uploads dist/ as an artifact and the rust legs `needs: client` and download it (or the Windows leg keeps its own build if the embed must differ per OS - to be measured).

## Flow
- client job: actions/upload-artifact dist/
- rust job: needs client; actions/download-artifact into apps/desktop/client/dist; drop its install+build steps
- compare CI wall time and runner minutes over two pushes before/after

## Expected impact
Fewer runner minutes and a shorter rust leg on every push. Risk: the rust legs now wait for the client job, so wall time can grow while minutes fall - measure both.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer duplicate client builds in CI
Before: 3 installs + 3 builds of the client per push (ci.yml:21,24 and :51,52 x a matrix of 2)
After: predicted 1 install + 1 build; wall time not measured
Method: simulation - only CI runs can time it and the file is outside this round's paths
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
.github/workflows/ci.yml:21 - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
.github/workflows/ci.yml:24 - run: pnpm build
.github/workflows/ci.yml:38 os: [windows-latest, ubuntu-latest]
.github/workflows/ci.yml:51-52 pnpm --dir apps/desktop/client install / build
instrument: two CI runs before and after: total runner minutes and end-to-end wall time

title: Retire legacy .amt and the console.css rule that exists only to undo it
body:
> Lane B unmeasurable: legacy .amt cascade needs a real-browser computed-style probe

## Summary

Claim: quality - no legacy cascade on v2 money
Before: rules touching v2 .amt: legacy 4 + reset 1
After: 0
Method: simulation - grep of drawers; jsdom has no layout

title: Frozen prototypes predate the words rules: vendor names and internals on screen
body:
## Summary
The prototypes still show a market-data vendor name (53 rendered occurrences in prototype/pages/*) and internals (Rust, MCP, env var names, REST paths) that the app words guards forbid. Whether frozen design records must obey the current words rules is an owner call.

## Description
UX-GUIDE: PayPal is the only vendor name; AGENTS.md: no vendor product names or internals in user-facing strings. This round removed the vendor name from the shared fixtures and the Dial (f95d70c), but 53 rendered occurrences remain inline in prototype/pages/* (other contexts), and prototype/main/modules.js still says "Checked in Rust" (:299), "no tools and no MCP servers" (:297), "$CLAUDE_CODE_BIN · found" (:863), "GET /v2/checkout/orders/…" (:557, :694). These are design records the owner chose on 6 Oct; rewriting them changes the record. Options: (a) mark the prototypes as pre-guard design records in the README / gallery lede and leave them; (b) run the words guard over prototype/ and conform them.

## Flow
- open any Shield/Tables/Setup variant -> the vendor name appears in rule lines and source cells
- open prototype/main -> Spend -> ⓘ on the gate -> "Checked in Rust"

## Expected impact
Decides whether a reviewer reading a prototype sees the same vocabulary as the app. Could break: (b) rewrites 39 owner-approved records.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one vocabulary across records and app
Before: 53 rendered vendor-name occurrences (jsdom probe over 39 pages), 5 internals sites in modules.js
After: (a) 53 with a label; (b) 0
Method: probe - jsdom render count; the choice between (a) and (b) is a direction call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
jsdom probe (text + title/aria/placeholder, modules and deals opened): TOTAL 57 before f95d70c, 53 after; top: pages/shield/variant-3 9, pages/shield/variant-1 7, pages/shield/variant-2 7, pages/tables/variant-2 7
prototype/main/modules.js:297,299,557,694,863

title: Decide a horizon for nonces_seen, whose exp is written and never read
body:
## Summary
Every stored envelope inserts a nonces_seen row with exp, nothing ever reads exp or deletes a row, and the nonce_expiry index is maintained for no query.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/migrations/0001_table.sql:31 and 0002_integrity.sql:7 (CREATE INDEX nonce_expiry ON nonces_seen(exp)); writer crates/table-ledger/src/negotiation.rs:146-149, reader negotiation.rs:17-24 (key_id, nonce only). verify_transcript replays with in-memory nonces (crates/table-ledger/src/transcript.rs), and verify() refuses an expired envelope, so a nonce past exp cannot be replayed anyway. Pruning deletes stored rows from the replay-protection table, which is an owner decision.

## Flow
- each OFFER/COUNTER/ACCEPT/SETTLE/RECEIPT/NOTE adds one row forever
- index nonce_expiry is updated on every insert and used by no query

## Expected impact
Bounded growth of a table that grows with every message; or, if kept, a dropped index and a stated reason.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the store states a horizon for replay nonces
Before: 1 column + 1 index written, 0 readers; 0 deletes
After: a stated horizon (prune past exp + skew) or the index dropped
Method: probe - grep of nonces_seen readers/writers (2 statements)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
instrument: count nonces_seen rows vs envelopes rows on a long-lived ledger copy; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN of the two nonce statements (nonce_expiry unused)

title: Retire schema states nothing writes: deals_closed, mandate 'expired', mandate kinds
body:
## Summary
The schema admits states no code reaches: counterparties.deals_closed is never written (always 0) because the list computes the count; mandates.status 'expired' is never set; mandates.kind 'rescue'/'shop' are never written (insert hard-codes 'open').

## Description
crates/table-ledger/migrations/0001_table.sql:13 deals_closed INTEGER DEFAULT 0 - no writer anywhere (grep), crates/table-ledger/src/display.rs:17 computes it from deals. 0001_table.sql:6 status CHECK includes 'expired'; writers set only 'superseded' and 'revoked' (crates/table-ledger/src/mandates.rs:168,211); expiry is judged on read. 0001_table.sql:2 kind CHECK ('open','rescue','shop'); crates/table-ledger/src/mandates.rs:171 inserts 'open' always. A reader that trusts these columns reads a value that is always the default.

## Flow
- grep deals_closed writers -> 0; grep status='expired' writers -> 0; grep kind values written -> 'open' only

## Expected impact
The schema stops promising states that never occur; any change is a migration on the merchant's single store.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every admitted state has a writer or is gone
Before: 3 admitted states/columns with 0 writers
After: 0
Method: probe - greps over crates/ for each writer
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
instrument: a schema test listing each CHECK value and asserting a production writer exists (grep-derived), seeded red by the three above

title: Correct 0001's column comments, pinned verbatim to the design report
body:
## Summary
0001_table.sql's comments describe shapes the code never writes, and the file is pinned verbatim to docs/design/the-table.html, so the fix is a design-report edit plus a migration-file edit.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/migrations/0001_table.sql:22 decided_by -- 'policy:clause6' | 'human:2026-..' (code writes canonical DecidedBy JSON; crates/table-ledger/src/repositories.rs:124-128 says so); :43 actor -- 'agent:buyer-1' | 'owner' | 'policy:clause6' | 'peer:47be..' (writers use 'policy', 'agent', 'pipeline', 'attention', 'house-witness', ...); :20 market_json -- Channel3 snapshot (a MarketRef). crates/table-ledger/src/tests.rs migration_0001_matches_report_html_verbatim compares the file to the report, so editing either alone goes red; editing an applied migration is a change to shipped schema text.

## Flow
- read 0001 comments against the writers named

## Expected impact
A reader of the DDL learns the real shapes; the report and the file move together.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - stated column shapes match the writers
Before: 3 comments describing unwritten shapes
After: 0
Method: probe - each comment checked against its writers
Result: better
Gate: irreversible
instrument: migration_0001_matches_report_html_verbatim stays green with report and file edited together

title: A partly paid rescue invoice expires uncounted and unflagged
body:
## Summary
A rescue invoice PayPal reports PARTIALLY_PAID is read as still waiting, then expires at its deadline like an unpaid one: money arrived, nothing counts it and nothing asks the owner.

## Description
crates/table-app/src/rescue.rs rescue_poll matches PAID (nothing due) and CANCELLED (:595); PARTIALLY_PAID falls to `_ => Ok(false)` (:599). At the deadline crates/table-app/src/rescue/deadline.rs:53-99 reads once more, gets Ok(false), then apply_deadline_default (:97) ends the deal EXPIRED. SENT_STATUSES (rescue.rs:93) already treats PARTIALLY_PAID as proof the send went out, so the code knows the state. What the product does with part of a discounted cycle (count it, flag it for the owner, keep reading) is a product decision the design (DECISIONS 13) does not state.

## Flow
- owner approves a fix; the subscriber pays part of the invoice
- rescue_poll reads PARTIALLY_PAID -> Ok(false), every cadence
- deadline: one more read, Ok(false), deal EXPIRED, rescue_recovered unchanged, no attention item

## Expected impact
The owner learns that a subscriber paid something instead of seeing an expired fix. Could break: recovered totals, if partial amounts are counted.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a partial payment is surfaced, not silently expired
Before: PARTIALLY_PAID -> EXPIRED with 0 rows saying money arrived (walked through rescue_poll and rescue_deadline)
After: depends on the chosen behaviour (count, attention, or keep reading)
Method: simulation - three walked cases; the target behaviour is a product choice
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
crates/table-app/src/rescue.rs:599 _ => Ok(false) after PAID / CANCELLED arms
crates/table-app/src/rescue.rs:93 SENT_STATUSES includes PARTIALLY_PAID
crates/table-app/src/rescue/deadline.rs:97 apply_deadline_default after an Ok(false) read
instrument: tests/rescue.rs: the Invoicing double answers PARTIALLY_PAID with due_amount > 0; assert the chosen outcome at the deadline (today: EXPIRED, rescue_recovered empty, no attention item)
